articles.title: The world is reacting to the Democrats' sweeping midterm elections victory
articles.author: Kate Bartlett

paras.en: The world is reacting to the Democrats' sweeping midterm elections victory

One color dominates international headlines about the U.S. midterm election results. French newspaper Libération called the Democrats' win "une vague bleue," or blue wave, Britain's Daily Mail dubbed it a "historic blue tsunami," and The Times of India's headline ran "midterm blues for Trump."

Countries at war were also watching closely, with Ukrainian newspaper The Kyiv Independent's online headline hopeful: "Democrats seize control of Congress in blow to Trump, potential boost for Ukraine."

Russia had a different take. Rossiyskaya Gazeta, the state-run daily newspaper, suggested the results would in fact be a blow to Ukraine, which has firm support from the European Union. "Brussels, brace yourself. After the Republicans' defeat, Trump's wrath will fall on Europe," read the headline.

Iran's Tehran Times said "Call it Operation Midterms Hammer" — a play on the U.S. military's Operation Midnight Hammer strikes against Iran in June 2025. Since the United States and Israel renewed their war against Iran this February, the fallout has pushed up the price of oil and other goods, becoming a major election campaign issue. The article ran a cartoon of a man slamming a mini-Trump with a hammer in a game of whack-a-mole.
In Israel, which just held its own parliamentary elections last week, headlines focused on what the Democrats' victory means for the U.S. support of the Jewish state and its war in Gaza.

The Times of Israel ran a headline focusing on Democrat Abdul El-Sayed's triumph in the U.S. Senate race in Michigan, saying "Anti-Israel El-Sayed wins Michigan Senate race, pledges no money for 'apartheid, genocide.'" A headline in Israel's Haaretz read: "Abdul El-Sayed Shows Opposition to Israel Is No Barrier to Winning Battleground States."
Newspapers in U.S. neighbors Canada and Mexico, meanwhile, noted the results were a rebuke and setback for Trump.
Some foreign politicians celebrate, others keep silent

International leaders tend to shy away from commenting directly on the results of U.S. midterm elections, as opposed to presidential races when they routinely congratulate the winner. However, this time several have made public statements.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said that with Trump accepting the midterms results, the focus can turn to ending wars and bringing down prices.

"The world has an opportunity now to unite around the issue that is affecting us all, and that's the cost of living," Burnham told reporters Wednesday. "I can't get people's cost of living pressures down until the conflict in the Middle East is resolved, the conflict in Ukraine started by Russia, these are the things we have to focus on now."
"I feel the world has an opportunity now to unite around the issue that is affecting us all - and that's the cost of living."
Reacting to the Democrats' victory over Trump's Republicans in the Senate, PM Andy Burnham says now is an opportunity to focus on other matters. pic.twitter.com/xkGl4eogSY
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, who has an acrimonious relationship with Trump, was forthright in his response.

"Yesterday, American society voted against policies that only impoverish. Against hate. Against machismo. Against climate denialism and against the privileges of the elites," Sánchez wrote on social media.

In South Africa, where diplomatic relations with the U.S. are at an all-time low after Trump falsely accused the government of persecuting its white minority, President Cyril Ramaphosa said "The people of America have spoken."

Ramaphosa made the comments as he cast his own ballot in South Africa's municipal elections Wednesday, adding: "I do think that this is going to introduce a new era in world relations. … We're hoping that on a bilateral basis there will be a coming together of minds."

A senior Russia diplomat suggested the Democratic Party's return to power in both houses of Congress bode ill for U.S.-Russian relations. "The approach of the activist wing of the Democratic Party towards Russia is extremely negative. There's nothing new in that," said Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov in an interview with the state RIA-Novosti news service. Ryabkov also signaled there would be no grand shifts in Russian foreign policy as a result.

In Germany, Defense Minister Boris Pistorius congratulated Democrats on an "historic victory," adding that Berlin's commitment to cooperating with the administration in Washington remains unchanged. He stressed that Berlin will be reaching out to both Democrats and Republicans.

Norway's Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stoere said the results are a "powerful political signal about a change of course among American voters." Speaking to Reuters, Stoere said "voices are now emerging in American politics that are closer to us than the president and the administration have stood for, for example on climate and environment, and in foreign policy and development aid policy."

A spokeswoman for China's Foreign Ministry told a daily press conference that the midterm elections "are an internal affair of the United States." She added that "China is willing to continue working with the U.S. to … strengthen communication, properly manage differences, expand cooperation, and build a constructive, strategically stable China-U.S. relationship based on the principles of respect, fairness, and reciprocity."

Japan's top government spokesman, Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara, told a news conference that Japan's alliance with the U.S. remains essential for global peace and stability, regardless of the outcome of midterm elections.

The alliance "remains the cornerstone of Japan's foreign and security policy" and is crucial to "maximizing its national interests" amid an increasingly volatile and uncertain global situation," he added.

Iran's Parliament Speaker and top negotiator Mohammad Baqer Ghalibaf commented on X: "Conscience or the cost of living, Americans said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message. If the US govt betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare."

For Israel, the U.S. midterm results fall during a time of political uncertainty, amid coalition-building talks after Trump's ally, incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, lost his parliamentary majority in Oct. 27 Israeli elections. "In some ways Netanyahu lost two elections in the last week," said Israel-American analyst Mairav Zonstein.

Netanyahu's rivals seized on the midterm results. One Israeli opposition leader, Yair Golan, said the U.S. results reveal "just how toxic Netanyahu is among both Democrats and Republicans." Another, Yair Lapid, said the U.S. results "eliminate any possibility of a unity government led by Netanyahu."

Laura Cain in London, Charles Maynes in Moscow, Esme Nicholson in Berlin, Lauren Frayer in Tel Aviv, Hadeel Al-Shalchi in Istanbul, Aya Batrawy in Dubai and Anthony Kuhn in Seoul contributed reporting.

articles.title: Abdul El-Sayed welcomes Trump's plan to cut Israel aid, calls for end to arms sales
articles.author: Steve Inskeep

paras.en: Abdul El-Sayed welcomes Trump's plan to cut Israel aid, calls for end to arms sales
Democrat Abdul El-Sayed made history in Michigan, defeating Republican Mike Rogers to become the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate as his party reclaimed control of Congress.

The 42-year-old former public health official campaigned on lowering costs, Medicare for All and getting corporate money out of politics. Rogers, backed by President Trump, repeatedly attacked El-Sayed over his Muslim faith and opposition to U.S. military aid to Israel.

But Israel and the war in Gaza became a defining fault line in the race. Haley Stevens, whom El-Sayed defeated in the Democratic primary, endorsed Rogers just days before the election amid a bitter dispute over Israel.
After a campaign marked by heated disagreements over Israel, El-Sayed now finds himself on the same side of an issue as Trump.
The president announced plans to end roughly $4 billion in annual military aid to Israel by the end of the year, though he offered no details on how the cuts would work.
Speaking to Morning Edition after his victory, El-Sayed welcomed the proposal.
"I think the president is actually right on this policy," he said. "I'd also like to see us stop selling weaponry that gets used to do the worst things, including genocide and apartheid, to Israel."
The U.S. provides Israel with $3.8 billion in annual military aid under an agreement that runs through 2028.
His argument goes beyond Israel. El-Sayed also questioned U.S. military support for Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Jordan and Pakistan, saying American tax dollars should be spent at home.
Winning Michigan's Senate seat, however, doesn't mean every division within his party has disappeared.

During a visit to Michigan before the election, NPR's Michel Martin heard concerns about El-Sayed from some Jewish and Black voters. Asked whether he still had work to do to win their support, El-Sayed said the election results challenged that narrative.
"There's always more work to do. There's always more to build. There's always more conversations to have," he said.
Listen to the full interview live by clicking on the blue button above.
The digital version was edited by Treye Green.

articles.title: NYC's Mamdani says Abdul El-Sayed's Senate victory in Michigan 'means so much to so many'

paras.en: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Wednesday that Abdul El-Sayed's Senate election victory in Michigan "is one that means so much to so many."
El-Sayed, who will become the first Muslim U.S. senator in history, toppled former Republican Rep. Mike Rogers in what was one of the most-watched contests of the election.

"I haven't spoken to him yet. I'm sure he is quite busy. I've had the privilege of speaking to him in the past, and I have to say that his election is one that means so much to so many," Mamdani said Wednesday.

"And to see to see that victory in the face that all that he had to reckon with over the course of that campaign, whether in terms of the extraordinary amount of money spent to oppose him or the racism and slander that he was met with on a daily basis, it is incredibly exciting to see as he said last night, that the good guys won," Mamdani added.
Mamdani added that "what last night showed us is that Americans are tired of being told that their needs are unrealistic by politicians who have been bought by the wealthiest people in the country.

"This country has elected a new generation of leadership, a generation with a mandate to lower the cost of living, to build, not bomb, to never betray the working people who entrusted them with power," he added. "And I hear often that the politics that we're fighting for here in New York City are not possible outside of city limits. And what last night showed us is that working people are the majority, whether we are speaking of Austin or Ann Arbor or Astoria, and it is time to put those same people first in our politics and last night shows us that it's possible to do so all across the country."
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Democrats regained control of the House and Senate during Tuesday's midterm elections, but Mamdani said that "it is not enough for us as Democrats to win power.

"We have to use that power to deliver change that Americans can feel in their wallets," he continued. "And to me, when you look at these campaigns, if we want to speak about James Talarico, he campaigned on a vision for universal childcare. If you want to talk about Keisha Lance Bottoms, well she campaigned on a vision of cutting red tape, to actually be able to build housing at the speed that's needed.

"If you want to talk about Jocelyn Benson, she campaigned on a moratorium for data centers. These, to me, are examples of the kind of specifics. But again, what I'm excited to see now is a recognition that the work is only just starting and that this has to be delivered for working people across the country," Mamdani declared.

articles.title: Warriors have reportedly stopped paying Kristaps Porzingis' $20 million salary amid mystery illness saga

paras.en: The Golden State Warriors have reportedly stopped paying former NBA champion Kristaps Porzingis by ruling that the 31-year-old is not rendering his services.

ESPN NBA insider Shams Charania has reported that, according to league sources, the franchise has ceased delivering the semimonthly payments he is due on his $20 million salary. The report also indicated that Porzingis is not actively disputing the lack of payments, and the NBA Players' Association has no plans to dispute it.

Porzingis has not taken the floor for the Warriors this season and stepped away from the team the day before the team's training camp began this offseason. The Latvian is reportedly dealing with recurring symptoms tied to Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome (POTS), which can cause dizziness and fatigue.
Porzingis addressed speculation about his health in an Oct. 14 post on X, and also spoke about online rumors involving "internet doctors" who alleged that he had contracted HIV or AIDS.

"Hello people, I’m working with doctors and experts to figure out how to be fully back to good health asap. Honestly, I’m getting better and better," he wrote on X. "I just have to stay patient, and I believe I’ll be feeling great again soon."
"I appreciate all the internet doctors trying to diagnose and help, but I’m in the best hands," he later wrote. "So everyone can relax now and I don’t have HIV or AIDS."

Despite appearing in just 74 total games over the last two seasons battling health issues, the Warriors opted to sign the big man to a two-year, $40 million extension during the offseason. Porzingis has earned more than $253 million in the NBA since making his debut as a New York Knick in 2015.
The former fourth-overall pick in the 2015 NBA Draft won a title with the Boston Celtics in 2024, averaging 12.3 points per game during the championship run.
After beginning the season with three consecutive losses, the Warriors are currently riding a five-game winning streak.

articles.title: Dan Dakich reacts to MS NOW host Joe Scarborough's Pat McAfee take: 'They look like idiots'

paras.en: While there are plenty of polarizing figures on television nowadays, there is perhaps no one who is more of a lightning rod than ESPN's very own Pat McAfee.
The former All-Pro punter for the Indianapolis Colts has become somewhat ubiquitous with The Worldwide Leader, appearing all over their many different channels seemingly at all hours of the day.
He is most well known for his work on "College Gameday," one of ESPN's most popular original programs, but lately his notoriety has turned to infamy thanks to the cries of several online "haters."

One of those haters just so happens to be MS NOW commentator (and Matthew Perry lookalike) Joe Scarborough, and although most political pundits were busy making sense of the midterm elections on Tuesday, the "Morning Joe" host took aim at the "Gameday" centerpiece.
Scarborough claims McAfee "ruined College Gameday" and that the supposed rejection of his antics are a rebuke of the "manosphere" that has been cultivated since 2024.
OutKick's Dan Dakich got a hold of this rant from Scarborough and had a few choice words for Mr. Morning Joe himself.

"Four dudes that know absolutely nothing about football are trying to chime in on social events that football people are talking about," Dakich said, referring to Scarborough and his fellow deskmates.
The "Don't @ Me" host notes that this feels painfully similar to Minnesota governor and noted manly man Tim Walz larping as a football dude during Kamala Harris' 2024 presidential campaign.
"This is just like little Timmy Walz trying to be a 'real boy,'" Dakich joked.
Dakich also corrected Scarborough for claiming that McAfee was "offended" by a few kids holding up signs.
Another big swing and a miss by a lib pretending to care about things normal dudes are into, which should come as a surprise to absolutely no one.
I hate to be the "stick to politics" guy, but maybe Scarborough should stay in his lane and leave the sports stuff to the ones who actually care about them.

articles.title: British healthcare worker with Ebola evacuated from DR Congo to UK
articles.author: Sarah Johnson

paras.en: A British healthcare worker with Ebola is being evacuated from the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the UK for medical treatment, it has been confirmed.

“A British citizen currently in the DR Congo has tested positive for Ebola,” a spokesperson for the UK government said in a statement on Wednesday. “The UK has well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this, and those processes have been activated … The risk to the UK public from Ebola remains low.”

The patient, whose identity is unknown, is in a stable condition and is expected to arrive in the UK on Wednesday or Thursday before being transferred in a specialist ambulance to a “high consequence” infectious disease unit, according to an official document seen by Reuters.

A humanitarian organisation sent the worker to DR Congo to help in the response to the outbreak, which is the second largest on record. It is the first case involving a British national contracting Ebola in the current outbreak.
The Royal Free hospital in London has a high-level isolation unit for infectious diseases such as Ebola; other centres are in Newcastle and Liverpool.
Ebola is a highly contagious, severe and often fatal illness. It is spread through direct contact with body fluids such as the blood or vomit of infected people, or dead bodies.

The current outbreak, declared on 15 May by DR Congo’s health ministry, has surpassed 10,000 cases, and 5,000 deaths. It is the 17th in DR Congo since Ebola was identified, was caused by the Bundibugyo virus, and has become the largest and deadliest in the country’s history. The Bundibugyo virus has no approved treatment, though vaccine trials are under way.

Since the outbreak started, it has spread to Kenya and Uganda in east Africa, while last month Nigeria confirmed a case in the capital, Abuja, after a woman who arrived from Uganda tested positive for the virus. She, along with a close contact, were evacuated to Switzerland for treatment.

In an interview with the Guardian last month, Dr Jean Kaseya, the director general of the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), said the “unprecedented” spread of the Ebola outbreak meant it could reach the UK and other countries.

“We want all countries to know that they are not safe if they don’t take appropriate measures,” he said. “Each country, not only in the African region, but all continents, must now increase the preparedness level and the possibility for treatment.
“It is the first time three African regions have been affected [by Ebola]. The geographic extension of this outbreak is unprecedented.”

Other patients who have been medically evacuated for specialised care since the start of the outbreak include two sent to Germany and one to the Netherlands. Another case was reported in France in July.
British health authorities say the risk to the wider public from imported Ebola cases remains low and the NHS has procedures in place to manage suspected and confirmed infections.
There have only been four confirmed cases recorded in Britain since 1976, according to the UK Health Security Agency.

articles.title: The midterms were a thumping rebuke of the US-Israel relationship
articles.author: Alice Speri

paras.en: On the eve of a midterm election that ended in an unequivocal rejection of his brand of politics, even Donald Trump seemed to recognize that the US-Israel relationship had become a political liability.

Trump’s 11th-hour suggestion, on election morning, that he would cut military aid to Israel at the end of the year because, as he put it, “they don’t need it”, was condemned across the board – with pro-Palestinian advocates dismissing it as “desperate” and pro-Israel ones as “unserious”.

Trump’s suggestion that he would replace nearly $4bn in annual military aid with arms sales signaled little would change in practice – the funding would continue and it would be harder to track. But it was still a notable recognition by the president of just how much support for Israel has tanked against the backdrop of the latest war in Gaza, which has killed more than 70,000 Palestinians, been widely been described as a genocide, and reshaped US politics in ways unthinkable just three years ago.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Indeed, come January, the US House will include an army doctor who went on a medical mission in Gaza, a lawyer who was fired by her firm over a blogpost criticizing Israel’s war, a Jewish lawmaker who was recently detained by Israeli forces while helping Palestinians harvest olives in the occupied West Bank, and a community organizer who participated in a pro-Palestine student encampment and scored one of the primary season’s most stunning upsets under the banner “babies, not bombs”.

Pro-Palestinian candidates – including Palestinian-American ones – have won downballot races. And in Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed became the first Muslim to be elected to the US Senate, following a campaign that saw more than $40m spent by Aipac in an effort to defeat him, last-minute drama, and unprecedented levels of Islamophobic rhetoric and bigotry.

“The old bipartisan consensus on Israel is over,” Beth Miller, political director of Jewish Voice for Peace Action, said. Without that consensus in place, the next Congress could push a number of measures, from an arms embargo on Israel to sanctions against violent settlers and officials – though Trump would retain veto power to block them.

The vote was also a rejection of Trump’s war in Iran – something even JD Vance said on Wednesday was “obvious to almost everyone”. Foreign policy issues rarely determine US elections – that is, until those issues have a direct effect on Americans’ lives at home.

“Americans were reminded of the failures of the Iran war with every visit to the gas station and grocery store,” said Yousef Munayyer, head of the Palestine/Israel Program at the Arab Center Washington DC. “Israel is a central piece of that story.”

Across the country, and up and down the ballot, unabashedly pro-Palestinian candidates defeated pro-Israel ones despite groups like Aipac pouring tens of millions of dollars into a failed attempt to reverse Israel’s collapsing standing among US voters. Last month, Aipac acknowledged its open support was hurting pro-Israel candidates more than it helped them, and announced it would stop making direct endorsements and contributions – a remarkable admission even if one with little practical consequence.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The victories of El-Sayed and several other candidates whom the right sought to cast as antisemitic over their support for Palestinians also marked a significant rejection of the narrative that pro-Israel voices and the Trump administration have relentlessly advanced over the last three years – that criticism of Israel is, by default, antisemitic.

“They try to call you hateful if you believe that Palestinian kids should get to grow up in the land of their forefathers without being murdered by our tax dollars,” El-Sayed, who has continued to speak plainly about his support for Palestinians despite coming under enormous pressure over it, said during his acceptance speech. “If you believe in equal rights to peace, dignity, and self determination, that’s not hate, it’s love.”

In Michigan, El-Sayed won a majority of Jewish voters, according to exit polls. Despite warnings that Jews would leave the Democratic party en masse over its shifts on Israel, J Street said its polling found that 72% of Jews voted for Democrats on Tuesday, even though the Republican party increased its share of the Jewish vote since 2024..
This does not mean that the Democratic party is unified on Israel and Palestine and or in opposition to foreign wars.

For decades, the party has “excluded or marginalized anyone whose progressive values extend to support for Palestine”, Lara Friedman, the president of the Foundation for Middle East Peace, said. “American voters, organizers, and a cohort of enormously talented candidates came together and kicked the door down.”

Matt Duss, executive vice-president of the Center for International Policy and a former foreign policy aide to Senator Bernie Sanders, said that the Democrats now must seize the opportunity to become the party opposed to war.

“Trump ran and won as an anti-war candidate in 2024, because unfortunately Democrats left that lane wide open for him,” he said. “The question is: will Democrats finally get it? Will they finally realize that Americans are tired of war and want a new foreign policy?”

articles.title: Mother and daughter both killed in grizzly bear attack, Canadian authorities confirm
articles.author: Leyland Cecco in Toronto

paras.en: Search teams in Canada have discovered the body of a 20-year-old woman and confirmed that both she and her mother were killed in an attack that conservation officers now believe could have involved multiple grizzly bears.
paras.zh: 加拿大的搜索小组发现了一名20岁女子的尸体，并确认她和她的母亲在一次袭击中丧生，保护官员现在认为这次袭击可能涉及多只灰熊。

paras.en: Late on Tuesday, conservation officers in British Columbia said the two women, who were reported missing over the weekend, were located near a trail a short distance from their home.
paras.zh: 周二晚些时候，不列颠哥伦比亚省的保护官员表示，周末据报失踪的两名妇女位于离家不远的小径附近。

paras.en: The discovery has shaken a community where, earlier in the year, a grizzly attacked a group of schoolchildren and their teachers.
paras.zh: 这一发现震惊了一个社区，今年早些时候，一只灰熊袭击了一群学童及其老师。

paras.en: “Our thoughts are with the families of the victims during this tragic time,” inspector Jeff Tyre said in a video posted online. Tyre later said the conservation service is probing the possibility that more than one bear was involved in the fatal attack.
paras.zh: 检查员Jeff Tyre在网上发布的视频中说： “在这个悲惨的时刻，我们与受害者家属同在。” Tyre后来表示，保护局正在调查不止一只熊参与致命袭击的可能性。

paras.en: “We appreciate people’s concerns and the desire to assist but it is critical the public stay out of the area – both due to the danger and to allow officers to do their work,” he said.
paras.zh: 他说： “我们感谢人们的关注和帮助的愿望，但由于危险和允许官员开展工作，公众远离该地区至关重要。”

paras.en: Jenny Balcarras, an art therapist, and her daughter Selah Reed were reported missing by relatives over the weekend. A family member posted on Facebook about them, later updating it after the conservation service announced the suspected attack to indicate that their vehicle had been found at a trailhead near Bella Coola, British Columbia. Balcarras’s remains were found first and Reed was located a day later.
paras.zh: 艺术治疗师Jenny Balcarras和她的女儿Selah Reed在周末被亲戚报告失踪。一名家庭成员在Facebook上发布了有关他们的信息，后来在保护局宣布可疑袭击事件后更新了这一信息，表明他们的车辆在不列颠哥伦比亚省贝拉库拉附近的小径上被发现。Balcarras的遗体首先被发现， Reed在一天后被找到。

paras.en: A fundraiser for Balcarras started by her family mourned a woman who had recently moved to Bella Coola, a community of roughly 2,100 people, for a new job and “to start a new chapter” of her life. She leaves behind three adult children and a grandchild.
paras.zh: 由她的家人发起的Balcarras筹款活动哀悼了一位最近搬到贝拉库拉（ Bella Coola ）的女性，贝拉库拉是一个约有2100人的社区，她想找到一份新工作，并“开始她人生的新篇章”。她留下了三个成年子女和一个孙子。

paras.en: “[Jenny] was working toward building a future and had not yet had the opportunity to establish savings or put aside funds to help her family with unexpected expenses such as these,” wrote relative Mary Melissa Smith. “Tragically, no one could have anticipated that her family would be faced with such an unimaginable loss.”
paras.zh: 亲戚玛丽·梅丽莎·史密斯（ Mary Melissa Smith ）写道： “[Jenny]正在努力建设未来，但还没有机会建立储蓄或储蓄资金，以帮助她的家人支付诸如此类的意外费用。” “可悲的是，没有人能预料到她的家人会面临如此难以想象的损失。”

paras.en: The family also mourned 20-year-old Selah, who had her “whole life ahead of her” before the attack.
paras.zh: 这家人还哀悼了20岁的Selah ，她在袭击前“一生都在她面前”。

paras.en: “She was only beginning her journey into adulthood, making this loss even more heartbreaking,” wrote Smith.
paras.zh: 史密斯写道： “她才刚刚开始成年之旅，这让这种损失更加令人心碎。”

paras.en: Both Balcarras and Reed had lived in communities in remote and rugged parts of the province, as well as time in Alaska.
paras.zh: Balcarras和Reed都居住在该省偏远和崎岖地区的社区，以及阿拉斯加的时间。

paras.en: The suspected attack happened at the Snooka West trail area, about 8km (4.97 miles) east of Bella Coola, on the province’s central coast.

Bella Coola, which sits at the end of a fjord along the province’s central coast, is a remote location, and abundant food sources mean that grizzly bears are a common sight in the region, which is informally known as the Great Bear rainforest.

Grizzly attacks in the province are exceedingly rare, but last November, 11 people, some as young as nine years old, were injured when a grizzly emerged from the forest near 4 Mile, a Nuxalk community, and attacked a school group on a lunch break alongside a walking trail. Despite an extensive search, the bear was never located.

Samuel Schooner, elected chief of the Nuxalk Nation, said on Tuesday: “Our thoughts are with the victim’s family as they learn of this tragic event.” Schooner said a trapping effort to find the bear was under way and asked media to refrain from contacting community members.
The province’s premier-designate, Lorne Doerkson, called the news “heartbreaking” and said he was thinking of the victims’ family and the Nuxalk Nation.
“At a time of such profound grief and uncertainty, my thoughts are with everyone who is hurting and with all those supporting one another through an incredibly difficult day.”

articles.title: Iran's chief negotiator says Americans voted 'no to war'

paras.en: Iran's chief negotiator in talks with the US has said that Americans voted "NO TO WAR", after President Donald Trump's Republican Party suffered a stunning defeat in the midterm elections.
paras.zh: 伊朗首席谈判代表在与美国的谈判中表示，在唐纳德特朗普总统的共和党在中期选举中遭遇惊人失败后，美国人投票“反对战争”。

paras.en: "We endorse this message," parliament speaker Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf wrote on X.
paras.zh: 议会议长穆罕默德·巴盖尔·加里巴夫（ Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf ）在X上写道： “我们支持这一信息。

paras.en: "If the US [government] betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare," he warned.
paras.zh: 他警告说： “如果美国[政府]背叛了他们为国际贿赂者和勒索者服务的公众意愿，它将了解到我们的'不'会带来一场噩梦。”

paras.en: Trump acknowledged on Tuesday that the poor results for Republican congressional candidates were partly due to the war and the related surge in petrol prices. But he insisted that he did not regret launching a joint attack with Israel on Iran in February.
paras.zh: 特朗普周二承认，共和党国会候选人的糟糕结果部分是由于战争和相关的汽油价格飙升。但他坚称，他并不后悔2月份与以色列对伊朗发动联合攻击。

paras.en: In an interview with Fox News, Trump said of the midterm results: "I think a part of it was Iran".
paras.zh: 特朗普在接受福克斯新闻采访时谈到了中期结果： “我认为部分原因是伊朗。”

paras.en: He went on to say: "People agree with what I'm doing on Iran but they really probably weren't willing to do the short term consequences of paying more for gasoline - I understand that."
paras.zh: 他接着说： “人们同意我在伊朗所做的事情，但他们真的可能不愿意为汽油支付更多的短期后果-我理解这一点。”

paras.en: Speaking separately to the BBC's US news partner, CBS News, Trump said the conflict would end "when I say it ends".
paras.zh: 特朗普单独与英国广播公司的美国新闻合作伙伴哥伦比亚广播公司新闻（ CBS News ）交谈时表示，冲突将在“我说结束时”结束。

paras.en: In recent weeks, Trump has warned that the US and Israel could return to all-out war after the midterms if a deal to end the conflict cannot be reached with Iran.
paras.zh: 最近几周，特朗普警告说，如果无法与伊朗达成结束冲突的协议，美国和以色列可能会在中期结束后恢复全面战争。

paras.en: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei - who has not been seen in public since he was reportedly seriously wounded in the same Israeli air strike on the first day of the war that killed his father and predecessor, Ali - said he did not expect US policy to change.
paras.zh: 伊朗最高领袖莫伊塔巴·哈梅内伊（ Mojtaba Khamenei ）表示，他预计美国的政策不会改变。据报道，哈梅内伊在战争的第一天就因以色列空袭而严重受伤，杀死了他的父亲和前任阿里。

paras.en: Khamenei released a statement saying anyone who thought there would be any change from American "hostility towards the Iranian nation" was "gravely mistaken".
paras.zh: 哈梅内伊发表声明说，任何认为美国“对伊朗国家的敌意”会有任何改变的人都是“严重错误的”。

paras.en: He also said the war would have "much wider dimensions" if it resumed.
paras.zh: 他还表示，如果恢复战争，战争将具有“更广泛的层面”。

paras.en: In a separate development on Wednesday, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said four oil tankers caught fire after hitting naval sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz.
paras.zh: 在周三的另一项事态发展中，伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队（ IRGC ）表示，四艘油轮在霍尔木兹海峡击中海军水雷后起火。

paras.en: The IRGC said two of the vessels were still burning, and two additional tankers had been intercepted, according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency. It said they were trying to travel through a prohibited southern route in the Strait of Hormuz.
paras.zh: 伊斯兰革命卫队表示，其中两艘船仍在燃烧，另有两艘油轮被拦截，据半官方的塔斯尼姆通讯社报道。它说，他们正试图通过霍尔木兹海峡的一条被禁止的南部路线。

paras.en: BBC Verify has been investigating the IRGC claims, and has not found any evidence that four tankers were destroyed.
paras.zh: BBC Verify一直在调查IRGC的说法，但没有发现任何证据表明四艘油轮被摧毁。

paras.en: The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) centre said a tanker was struck by two unknown projectiles about 14 nautical miles (26km) north-east of Limah, in Oman's Musandam peninsula, on Tuesday evening. No casualties were reported, it added.
paras.zh: 英国海上贸易业务（ UKMTO ）中心表示，周二晚上，一艘油轮在阿曼穆桑丹半岛利马东北约14海里（ 26公里）处被两枚不明弹击中。它补充说，没有人员伤亡的报告。

paras.en: On Monday, an Indian crew member of a dhow - a wooden sailing boat - was killed in an attack north-east of Limah. Thirteen other crew members were rescued by Omani authorities.
paras.zh: 周一，一艘单桅帆船（一艘木制帆船）的印度船员在利马东北部的一次袭击中丧生。另有13名船员被阿曼当局救出。

paras.en: The IRCG also reported on Wednesday that its forces had shot down another US MQ-9 drone over the Strait of Hormuz.
paras.zh: IRCG周三还报告说，其部队在霍尔木兹海峡上空击落了另一架美国MQ-9无人机。

paras.en: It made a similar claim on Monday night, when US officials said the US military had carried out limited strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island in response to the IRGC firing on a US aircraft.
paras.zh: 它在周一晚上提出了类似的主张，当时美国官员表示，美国军方对伊朗的格什姆岛进行了有限的打击，以回应伊斯兰革命卫队对美国飞机的射击。

paras.en: In an interview with the Financial Times ahead of the midterms, Trump suggested he was happy with the state of the conflict, and that he did not consider them to be "really in a war".
paras.zh: 特朗普在中期选举前接受英国《金融时报》采访时表示，他对冲突现状感到满意，并不认为他们“真的处于战争状态”。

paras.en: When asked about what the newspaper described as "strong hints" by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu that there would be an attack on Iran this week, Trump said they were "locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no need for it".
paras.zh: 当被问及该报称以色列总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡（ Benjamin Netanyahu ）本周将对伊朗发动袭击的“强烈暗示”时，特朗普表示，如果我们需要离开，他们“被锁定并上膛，但可能没有必要”。

paras.en: Indirect talks to end the conflict have been stalled for months.
paras.zh: 结束冲突的间接谈判已经停滞了几个月。

paras.en: President Masoud Pezeshkian maintained on Tuesday that his government had been trying to resolve the crisis "through dialogue".
paras.zh: 总统马苏德·佩泽什基安（ Masoud Pezeshkian ）周二坚称，他的政府一直在努力“通过对话”解决危机。

paras.en: "No-one will benefit from this war" if it were to resume, he warned.
paras.zh: 他警告说，如果恢复这场战争， “没有人会从中受益”。

paras.en: He also emphasised that Iran's supreme leader had granted the government powers to negotiate "issues that he had previously considered off-limits".
paras.zh: 他还强调，伊朗最高领导人已授予政府就“他以前认为是禁区的问题”进行谈判的权力。

paras.en: Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqai said on Monday that the basis of the current indirect negotiations mediated by Qatar remained a seven-step proposal that Iran submitted in September. But he added that the proposal had been "condensed, making it possible to implement it within two days".
paras.zh: 伊朗外交部发言人Esmaeil Baqai周一表示，目前由卡塔尔调解的间接谈判的基础仍然是伊朗在9月份提交的七步建议。但他补充说，该提案已经“简化，可以在两天内实施”。

paras.en: The Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global oil and gas shipments usually pass, was effectively closed after the start of the Iran war due to Iranian missile and drone attacks on commercial vessels and the US naval blockade.
paras.zh: 由于伊朗导弹和无人机袭击商业船只以及美国海军封锁，在伊朗战争开始后，霍尔木兹海峡实际上已经关闭，全球五分之一的石油和天然气运输通常通过该海峡。

paras.en: The US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the war and reopen the Strait in June, but it collapsed within weeks after Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated its blockade.
paras.zh: 美国和伊朗于6月达成了结束战争和重新开放海峡的初步协议，但在伊朗恢复对航运的攻击以及美国恢复封锁后，该协议在几周内崩溃。

paras.en: Iran insisted it would not give up some measure of control over the waterway and began targeting vessels using a southern route through Omani waters that avoids its preferred route through Iranian waters.
paras.zh: 伊朗坚称，它不会放弃对水道的某种程度的控制，并开始使用通过阿曼水域的南部航线瞄准船只，该航线避开了通过伊朗水域的首选航线。

paras.en: To keep exports flowing from Gulf Arab states, the US military has been providing protection for tankers shuttling oil through the Strait of Hormuz.
paras.zh: 为了保持海湾阿拉伯国家的出口，美国军方一直在为穿梭于霍尔木兹海峡的油轮提供保护。

paras.en: Additional reporting by Gabriela Pomeroy
paras.zh: Gabriela Pomeroy的补充报道

articles.title: Ukraine says bodycam video shows deadly Russian double-tap bombing

paras.en: A bodycam video has been released by Ukraine police they say shows the moments between two powerful Russian bomb strikes that killed at least 40 people at an aid centre and a shelter.
paras.zh: 乌克兰警方发布了一段人体摄像头视频，他们说这段视频显示了两次强大的俄罗斯炸弹袭击之间的时刻，两次袭击在一个援助中心和一个避难所造成至少40人死亡。

paras.en: The footage, from a camera on one of the killed police officers, shows residents of the southern village of Kamyshuvakha going to an underground shelter after the first attack on Monday. Soon after a blast is heard and flames are seen as the shelter is hit.
paras.zh: 这段镜头来自一名遇难警察的摄像头，显示南部村庄Kamyshuvakha的居民在周一的第一次袭击后前往地下避难所。在听到爆炸声后不久，当避难所被击中时，就会看到火焰。

paras.en: President Volodymyr Zelensky said more than 30 people may still be under the rubble, as a search operation continued for the third day.
paras.zh: 总统沃洛季米尔·泽伦斯基（ Volodymyr Zelensky ）表示，随着搜查行动持续第三天，可能仍有30多人在废墟下。

paras.en: Nine gliding bombs, some weighing 3,000kg, hit the village as people had gathered to get humanitarian aid, Ukraine said.
paras.zh: 乌克兰说，当人们聚集在一起获得人道主义援助时，九枚滑翔炸弹击中了村庄，其中一些重达3000公斤。

paras.en: The bodycam footage was released by Ukraine's national police on Wednesday.
paras.zh: 乌克兰国家警察周三发布了身体摄像头镜头。

paras.en: It shows huge devastation after the first bomb strike on the village in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, as shocked local residents stare at the rubble.
paras.zh: 在乌克兰扎波罗热地区的村庄遭受第一次炸弹袭击后，震惊的当地居民凝视着瓦砾，这显示了巨大的破坏。

paras.en: Severely damaged buildings are also seen.
paras.zh: 还可以看到严重受损的建筑物。

paras.en: A voice of a military official is then heard on a two-way radio warning police on the ground of more glide bombs being launched towards Kamyshuvakha.
paras.zh: 然后，在地面上的双向无线电警告警方，向Kamyshuvakha发射了更多的滑翔炸弹，听到了一名军官的声音。

paras.en: "Quickly [go] to the shelter!" one of the police officers tells local residents, who are seen walking into the shelter - at least two floors underground.
paras.zh: “赶快[去]避难所！”一名警察告诉当地居民，有人看到他们走进避难所--至少在地下两层。

paras.en: Seconds later the shelter is hit, and the recording stops.
paras.zh: 几秒钟后，庇护所被击中，录音停止。

paras.en: Ukraine said the shelter was near a local school, which was being used to distribute humanitarian aid.
paras.zh: 乌克兰表示，该避难所位于当地一所学校附近，用于分发人道主义援助物资。

paras.en: BBC Verify has confirmed the video was filmed in the same place as footage released by the Ukrainian state emergencies service DSNS showing the aftermath Monday's attack in Komyshuvakha.
paras.zh: BBC Verify证实，该视频是在乌克兰国家紧急服务DSN发布的同一地点拍摄的，显示了周一在Komyshuvakha发生的袭击事件。

paras.en: In a post on social media on Wednesday, Zelensky said that "nine aerial bombs were dropped by the Russians.
paras.zh: 泽伦斯基周三在社交媒体上发帖称， “俄罗斯人投下了9枚空中炸弹。

paras.en: "First, they hit people who came to receive humanitarian aid, and then rescuers and police officers who arrived at the scene."
paras.zh: “首先，他们袭击了前来接受人道主义援助的人，然后袭击了到达现场的救援人员和警察。”

paras.en: The Ukrainian president added that "unfortunately, there has been very little reaction from the world to this insane attack", describing it as yet another of "thousands" of war crimes committed by Russia.
paras.zh: 乌克兰总统补充说， “不幸的是，世界对这次疯狂袭击的反应很少” ，将其描述为俄罗斯犯下的“成千上万”的战争罪行中的又一次。

paras.en: Ukraine's DSNS earlier posted another video showing a huge crater left after the attack on Kamyshuvakha.
paras.zh: 乌克兰的DSNs早些时候发布了另一段视频，显示了袭击Kamyshuvakha后留下的巨大火山口。

paras.en: The Russian military has not publicly commented.
paras.zh: 俄罗斯军方尚未公开发表评论。

paras.en: Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
paras.zh: 俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京于2022年2月发动了对乌克兰的全面入侵。

paras.en: Additional reporting Paul Brown, BBC Verify
paras.zh: BBC Verify的Paul Brown补充报道

articles.title: US midterm results a 'victory' for Canadians hopeful of tariff relief

paras.en: It was the midterm result that many in Canada had hoped for - a Democratic sweep that was in part a repudiation by American voters of Donald Trump's tariff on close trade allies.
paras.zh: 这是加拿大许多人所希望的中期结果--民主党的席卷部分是美国选民对唐纳德·特朗普对亲密贸易盟友征收关税的否定。

paras.en: "I was doing cartwheels down the street," said Ontario Premier Doug Ford on Wednesday morning, calling it "a victory for Canada".
paras.zh: 安大略省省长道格·福特（ Doug Ford ）周三早上说： “我正在街上做车轮，”称这是“加拿大的胜利”。

paras.en: Tuesday night's result is unlikely to grant Canada relief from those tariffs any time soon, but there is anticipation that the political shifts could create a more favourable environment for Ottawa to get the best deal now that on-again-off-again trade talks are back on.
paras.zh: 周二晚上的结果不太可能在短期内给予加拿大这些关税的减免，但预计政治转变可能会为渥太华创造一个更有利的环境，以便在贸易谈判重新开始后获得最佳协议。

paras.en: US voters cited affordability as a main concern heading into the midterms and a survey by the Cato Institute in September, external suggested that about 75% believe the tariffs have raised prices.
paras.zh: 美国选民认为可负担性是进入中期的主要担忧，卡托研究所9月份的一项调查显示，约75%的选民认为关税提高了价格。

paras.en: In states like Maine and Michigan, tariffs played a significant role in the hard-fought races.
paras.zh: 在缅因州和密歇根州等州，关税在激烈的竞争中发挥了重要作用。

paras.en: In Maine, incumbent Republican Senator Susan Collins clashed with the White House over tariffs.
paras.zh: 在缅因州，现任共和党参议员苏珊·柯林斯（ Susan Collins ）与白宫就关税问题发生冲突。

paras.en: She successfully lobbied to have some duties that directly affected the state removed, including on road salt, refrigeration equipment and seaweed, but in the end lost to Democrat Troy Jackson.
paras.zh: 她成功地游说取消了一些直接影响该州的职责，包括道路盐、制冷设备和海藻，但最终输给了民主党人特洛伊·杰克逊。

paras.en: A similar story played out in Michigan, where state's the automobile manufacturing industry is deeply intertwined with Canada's - and where Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed defeated Republican Mike Rogers.
paras.zh: 密歇根州发生了类似的故事，该州的汽车制造业与加拿大的汽车制造业密切相关，民主党候选人阿卜杜勒·埃尔·赛义德击败了共和党人迈克·罗杰斯。

paras.en: In Ohio, Senator-elect Sherrod Brown, who defeated Republican Jon Husted, called the levies a "disaster" and vowed to slash costs for voters by getting rid of them, external.
paras.zh: 在俄亥俄州，当选参议员谢罗德·布朗（ Sherrod Brown ）击败了共和党人乔恩·哈斯特德（ Jon Husted ） ，称这些关税是一场“灾难” ，并发誓要通过摆脱外部关税来削减选民的成本。

paras.en: Democratic leaders like Hakeem Jeffries and Chuck Schumer, now newly empowered, have both pushed to rein in the tariffs on Canada in recent months.
paras.zh: 最近几个月，像哈基姆·杰弗里斯（ Hakeem Jeffries ）和查克·舒默（ Chuck Schumer ）这样的民主党领导人都推动了控制对加拿大的关税。

paras.en: Still, Democratic control of Congress might not do much to move the needle on tariffs. Trump's levies have been largely enacted using executive orders without approval from Congress.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，民主党对国会的控制可能不会在关税问题上发挥多大作用。特朗普的征税主要是在未经国会批准的情况下使用行政命令颁布的。

paras.en: And speaking to Fox News on Tuesday night, Trump touted his "ultimate power" of veto to shut down bills passed by Congress that he does not like.
paras.zh: 周二晚上，特朗普对福克斯新闻(Fox News)发表讲话，吹嘘他有否决国会通过的他不喜欢的法案的“终极权力”。

paras.en: Some Democratic lawmakers have also supported certain tariffs in the past as a way to protect American manufacturing jobs, and could back keeping some in place.
paras.zh: 一些民主党议员过去也支持将某些关税作为保护美国制造业就业的一种方式，并可能支持保留一些关税。

paras.en: There are currently several layers of tariffs on Canada, notably on sectors like autos, steel, aluminium and forestry.
paras.zh: 目前对加拿大征收多层关税，特别是对汽车、钢铁、铝和林业等行业征收关税。

paras.en: After trade talks between Ottawa and Washington collapsed in August, the Trump administration imposed an additional 50% tariff on $20bn (Â£15bn) worth of various Canadian goods, from dairy to cosmetics and furniture.
paras.zh: 在渥太华和华盛顿之间的贸易谈判在8月份破裂后，特朗普政府对价值200亿美元（ 150亿英镑）的各种加拿大商品（从乳制品到化妆品和家具）征收了50%的额外关税。

paras.en: The US also declared a total import ban on motorcycles, whey protein and alcohol.
paras.zh: 美国还宣布全面禁止进口摩托车、乳清蛋白和酒精。

paras.en: Canada retaliated by slapping the US with its own 50% "dollar-for-dollar" tariffs. Most provinces have also banned the sale of US alcohol in retaliation.
paras.zh: 加拿大通过对美国征收50%的“美元对美元”关税来进行报复。为了报复，大多数省份也禁止销售美国酒精饮料。

paras.en: Trump had also previously threatened to escalate the trade war with Canada further by â raising tariffs on sectors, including auto manufacturing, as of 1 January.
paras.zh: 特朗普此前还威胁要通过从1月1日起提高包括汽车制造业在内的行业关税来进一步升级与加拿大的贸易战。

paras.en: There were signs that his administration had become more sensitive to the optics of its tariffs on Canada in the run up to the election.
paras.zh: 有迹象表明，在选举前夕，他的政府对其对加拿大的关税变得更加敏感。

paras.en: Just a few days before the vote, Trump told reporters that a trade deal is "very close" after speaking with Prime Minister Mark Carney.
paras.zh: 就在投票前几天，特朗普告诉记者，在与总理马克·卡尼(Mark Carney)交谈后，贸易协议“非常接近”。

paras.en: Speaking to reporters on Tuesday evening, Carney said of US negotiators that "they're asking less and they're offering more" in recent discussions.
paras.zh: 周二晚上，卡尼在谈到美国谈判代表时说，在最近的讨论中， “他们的要求更少，提供更多”。

paras.en: On Wednesday, US-Canada Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc said the midterm results won't change anything in the short term, and dismissed speculation over what the new Congress might do when they're seated in the new year as "an interesting discussion at a faculty club luncheon".
paras.zh: 周三，美国-加拿大贸易部长多米尼克·勒布朗（ Dominic LeBlanc ）表示，中期结果短期内不会改变任何事情，并驳斥了有关新国会在新年就职时可能采取什么措施的猜测，认为这是“教师俱乐部午餐会上的有趣讨论”。

paras.en: "Our approach will not change and we don't intend to speculate on the approach being taken by the Americans," he said.
paras.zh: “我们的方法不会改变，我们不打算推测美国人正在采取的方法，”他说。

paras.en: Pierre Poilievre, leader of Canada's Conservatives, said on Wednesday that "nobody controls Donald Trump".
paras.zh: 加拿大保守党领袖皮埃尔·波利耶夫尔（ Pierre Poilievre ）周三表示， “没有人控制唐纳德·特朗普”。

paras.en: But he said that midterms results show Canada has "massive leverage" given that the tariffs are broadly unpopular.
paras.zh: 但他表示，中期结果显示，鉴于关税普遍不受欢迎，加拿大具有“巨大的杠杆作用”。

paras.en: "We've got to use that goodwill to pressure for tariff-free trade," he said.
paras.zh: “我们必须利用这种善意来对免关税贸易施加压力，”他说。

paras.en: Trump may indeed feel more pressure to sign a deal with Canada now that American voters have clearly communicated their frustration, said Colin Robertson, a former Canadian diplomat and a fellow at the Canadian Global Affairs Institute.
paras.zh: 前加拿大外交官、加拿大全球事务研究所研究员科林·罗伯逊（ Colin Robertson ）表示，由于美国选民已经明确表达了他们的沮丧情绪，特朗普可能会感到与加拿大签署协议的压力更大。

paras.en: "Will this change Trump's mind? It might, because he suffered such a beating at the polls."
paras.zh: “这会改变特朗普的想法吗？也许吧，因为他在民意测验中遭到了如此的殴打。”

paras.en: But he added it remains to be seen how Trump will react from the bruising midterm loss.
paras.zh: 但他补充说，特朗普将如何应对瘀伤的中期损失还有待观察。

paras.en: Canada has an ideal window between now and January - when the new Democratic lawmakers are sworn in - to finalise a deal, Robertson noted.
paras.zh: 罗伯逊指出，从现在到1月份（新民主党议员宣誓就职） ，加拿大有一个理想的窗口来敲定一项协议。

paras.en: After that, Trump is likely to be distracted by investigations launched by Democrats into Trump's family and finances and some members of his administration, Robertson said.
paras.zh: 罗伯逊说，在那之后，特朗普可能会因为民主党人对特朗普的家庭和财务状况以及他的政府的一些成员发起的调查而分心。

paras.en: US trade representative Jamieson Greer also said earlier this year that he had ambitions to have interim deals in place with Canada and Mexico around the North American free trade deal, known as the USMCA in the US and CUSMA in Canada, before the end of the year.
paras.zh: 美国贸易代表杰米森·格里尔（ Jamieson Greer ）今年早些时候还表示，他希望在年底之前与加拿大和墨西哥就北美自由贸易协定（在美国称为USMCA ，在加拿大称为CUSMA ）达成临时协议。

paras.en: And while Carney struck a more optimistic tone in recent days on the current state of Canada-US trade talks, he also told Politico last month that he was prepared to wait for a new American president if necessary to reach a deal with the US.
paras.zh: 虽然卡尼最近几天对加拿大-美国贸易谈判的现状表达了更乐观的态度，但他上个月也告诉Politico ，如果有必要，他准备等待新的美国总统与美国达成协议。

articles.title: How Paper-Based Friction Materials Power Modern Machinery

paras.en: How Paper-Based Friction Materials Power Modern Machinery

Have you ever wondered what enables everything from roaring construction machinery to agricultural machinery plowing the fields to industrial equipment shuttling through factories—the precise starting, smooth operation, and reliable braking they achieve?

The answer lies in a seemingly insignificant yet crucial core component: friction material. It acts as the "safety guard" and "power link" of machinery, ensuring every brake is safe and effective, and every power transmission is smooth and flawless.

Among the vast family of friction materials, wet friction materials are becoming the new favorite in modern machinery due to their exceptional reliability, safety, and exceptionally long lifespan. Among wet materials, paper-based friction materials stand out as a leading force thanks to their excellent overall performance, cost-effectiveness, and broad application prospects.
Today, let's delve deeper into the fascinating world of this "unsung hero"—paper-based friction materials.
What is Paper-Based Friction Material? — A Sponge-Like Power Core
Imagine a "sponge" with countless tiny pores—that's the most intuitive image of paper-based friction material.

It is a material with a reticular porous structure composed of three core components: reinforcing fibers, functional fillers, and a binder resin. This unique structure gives it extraordinary capabilities:
- Oil Storage Capacity: The porous structure acts like a miniature "oil depot," capable of storing large quantities of lubricant.

- Dynamic Lubrication: When the friction plate and mating plate engage and are subjected to pressure, the lubricant within the material is instantly squeezed onto the friction surface, forming a tough lubricant film, enabling smooth, gentle "wet" friction.
- Self-Recovery: When the friction plates separate, the material rebounds like memory foam, "absorbing" the lubricant back into the pores, ready for the next operation.

It is this dynamic cycle of "oil storage-oil squeezing-oil return" that allows paper-based friction materials to perform well in an oil bath environment, achieving a perfect combination of high durability and stable friction performance.
Exploring Core Performance: How Do Three Key Factors Affect It?

The performance of paper-based friction materials is not static. Like a top athlete, its performance is influenced by the "field," "equipment," and "condition." Let's examine how these three key factors shape its performance.
Factor 1: The "Stage Effect" of Lubricants

Paper-based friction materials are highly sensitive to lubricants, and different lubricants create distinct "stages" for their performance. Even the same friction material can exhibit significantly different friction characteristics (especially the kinetic friction coefficient) when exposed to different lubricants.
Figure 1: Kinetic friction coefficient curve for a paper-based friction material in gear oil
Figure 2: Dynamic friction coefficient curve of the same material in hydraulic oil

Interpretation: The above chart clearly shows that the same material behaves very differently in gear oil and hydraulic fluid. Furthermore, various additives added to lubricating oils (such as dispersants and anti-wear agents) can interact complexly with the material surface, further affecting its friction properties. Therefore, choosing the right oil for paper-based friction materials is the first step in achieving optimal performance.
Density is a trump card for paper-based friction materials. It is directly related to the material's porosity, leading to a delicate balancing act in terms of performance.

High density (low porosity) means a denser material, resulting in better strength and thermal conductivity, lower wear rate, and longer life. However, the downside is reduced oil storage capacity, which can lead to a lower coefficient of friction and compromise power transmission.

Low density (high porosity) means the material is more porous, resulting in greater oil storage capacity and a higher coefficient of friction, which can provide greater braking force or transmit torque. However, the downside is reduced mechanical strength and wear resistance, shortening service life.
Figure 3: Comparison of the dynamic coefficient of friction for materials of varying densities (Type 2 to Type 6, increasing density)
Figure 4: Comparison of wear rates of materials with different densities

Interpretation: Figures 3 and 4 vividly illustrate this balancing act. There's no such thing as absolute good or bad, only suitability. When selecting a paper-based friction material, the optimal trade-off between friction coefficient and durability must be determined based on specific application requirements (e.g., high torque versus long life).
Factor 3: Extreme Challenges of Operating Conditions

In addition to oil type and density, actual operating conditions, such as surface pressure, sliding speed, and oil temperature, pose extreme challenges to paper-based friction materials. These factors directly affect the temperature of the friction interface, the thickness and stability of the oil film, and thus dynamically alter the coefficient of friction.

Therefore, please remember: the coefficient of friction of a particular paper-based friction material is not a fixed value, but rather a performance range determined through extensive and repeated testing under specific operating conditions.
Broad Applications: Injecting a Powerful "Heart" into Machinery

Thanks to its excellent overall performance and customizability, Carlisle Brake & Friction's paper-based friction materials have been successfully applied to the core components of various heavy-duty machinery, becoming their powerful and reliable "heart."
We understand that different machines and applications require significantly different friction materials. For example:
- Service brakes for construction machinery (such as excavators and loaders) require materials that provide a stable, powerful braking force under high loads to ensure safety.
- Powershift transmissions for agricultural machinery (such as tractors) require materials that provide smooth engagement and excellent heat resistance to handle frequent shifting.
- Clutches for industrial machinery require materials that respond quickly and have a long lifespan to ensure continuous and efficient operation of production lines.

To this end, Carlisle Brake & Friction has developed a series of special paper-based friction materials for different application scenarios, providing each customer with the most suitable and reliable solution.
Continuous Innovation, Driving the Future
Technological advancement is endless. To meet increasingly demanding application requirements and broaden market prospects, Carlisle Brake & Friction remains at the forefront of innovation.

We are not only continuously optimizing the formulation and processing of paper-based friction materials to push their performance limits, but are also actively exploring next-generation wet friction materials with even higher performance. These R&D efforts have made significant progress, aiming to provide global customers with more diverse and advanced options, driving the infinite possibilities of future machinery.

articles.title: Celebrating 100-Years with Medina Mayor and Employees

paras.en: Celebrating 100-Years with Medina Mayor and Employees

MEDINA, OHIO — September 24, 2025 — Carlisle Brake & Friction (CBF), a global leader in the development and manufacture of high-performance brake and friction solutions, today welcomed Medina Mayor Dennis Hanwell, Economic Development Director Kimberly Marshall, and Executive Director of the Medina Chamber of Commerce Jaclyn Ringstmeier, for a special photo op at the company’s headquarters, located at 920 Lake Road. The event was a commemorative celebration of CarlisleCBF’s 100-year anniversary and its enduring presence in the Medina community.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The photo op featured Mayor Hanwell alongside Carlisle’s Operations Leader, David Smith, and a number of employees who have been with the company for decades. The occasion honored CarlisleCBF’s century of innovation and its deep roots in the Medina area, where it has been a significant employer and community partner.

"We are incredibly proud of our history and our strong connection to the city of Medina," said David Smith. "This milestone is a testament to the hard work and dedication of our employees, many of whom have been with us for decades. We are grateful for the continued support of Mayor Hanwell and the entire Medina community."

The photo op followed a recent employee and family event at the Medina plant that celebrated the 100-year milestone. The celebration was filled with games, face painting, food, and fun for all ages, reinforcing the company's commitment to its employees and their families.

Mayor Hanwell expressed his gratitude for CarlisleCBF’s presence in the city. “Carlisle has been a part of the Medina community for nearly 65 years, providing good jobs and a strong economic foundation,” said Mayor Hanwell. "We are proud to celebrate their 100-year anniversary and recognize the significant role they have played in our city’s growth and prosperity."
CarlisleCBF, a brand of CentroMotion, was founded in 1925 and has grown to become a global leader in its field, serving a wide range of markets including agriculture, construction, and mining.

Carlisle Brake & Friction, a CentroMotion brand, is a leading global provider of highly engineered and integrated brake and friction solutions for a wide range of industrial applications. With over 100 years of experience, the company is dedicated to delivering innovative, reliable, and high-performance products to its customers worldwide.

articles.title: Fix Auto Washington Supports Local Students Through Hoodfest Car Show Sponsorship
articles.author: Jason Stahl

paras.en: Fix Auto USA recognized Fix Auto Washington for its participation in the 8th Annual Hoodfest Car Show, held Oct. 10 at Dixie Technical College in St. George, Utah.

Owned and operated by Dakota Lourenco, Fix Auto Washington sponsored the community event, which raises awareness and support for Dixie Technical College students. The show featured a wide variety of vehicles and drew community members, families and car enthusiasts from across the region.

As part of its sponsorship, the Fix Auto Washington team hosted a booth where attendees could connect with collision repair professionals, participate in a “Guess the Repair Cost” game, and receive Matchbox cars and giveaways.

“Events like Hoodfest provide a great opportunity to connect with the community while supporting the next generation of skilled trades professionals,” said Dakota Lourenco, owner of Fix Auto Washington. “We enjoyed meeting attendees, talking about the collision repair industry and sharing our passion for automotive repair. Most importantly, we’re proud to support an event that helps create opportunities for students pursuing careers in the trades.”
The sponsorship reflects Fix Auto Washington’s commitment to community engagement and workforce development within the Fix Auto USA network.

“Dakota and the Fix Auto Washington team demonstrate what it means to be actively involved in the communities they serve,” said Damien Reyna, COO, Driven Brands Collision Group. “Their participation in the Hoodfest Car Show not only helped create a fun and engaging experience for attendees, but also supported students exploring careers in the skilled trades. We are proud to recognize their commitment to giving back and strengthening connections within their local community.”
For more information visit FixAutoUSA.com.

articles.title: SEMA Announces 2026 New Product Award Winners
articles.author: Jason Stahl

paras.en: The Specialty Equipment Market Association (SEMA) announced the winners of its 2026 SEMA Show New Product Awards. The awards recognize outstanding new aftermarket products being brought to market and featured in the New Products Showcase in Lower South Hall booth no. 41271.
More than 1,300 products competed for top honors across 15 New Products Showcase categories. Judges selected one winner and two runners-up in each category.

“The SEMA Show New Product Awards celebrate the ingenuity driving the automotive aftermarket forward,” said Mike Spagnola, CEO of SEMA. “This year’s honorees demonstrate how our industry continues to anticipate customer needs and turn bold ideas into market-ready products.”

Entries were evaluated on innovation, manufacturing quality, consumer appeal, marketability and technical achievement. Together, the honorees offer insight into the emerging technologies, consumer demands and trends expected to influence vehicle customization, performance and personalization in 2027.

articles.title: Intrepid and Kinetic program will give premium discounts for ADAS procedures performed
articles.author: Teresa Moss

paras.en: A new program launched by Intrepid Direct and Kinetic ID could reduce business insurance costs for collision repair shops that recognize and complete ADAS procedures.

Nikhil Naikal, CEO and co-founder of Kinetic, told Repairer Driven News that the software is used by shops and insurance carriers to identify ADAS requirements when vehicles have been in a collision or if they had a mechanical repair done.

“Sensors on the vehicles can be disrupted or dislodged during the process of a repair and the requirements of calibrations are not very easy to know or understand,” Naikal said. “It is a hidden digital damage. Kinetic ID is a software that helps identify when reprogramming and calibrations are required.”
Intrepid Direct, which provides business insurance to collision repair facilities, have identified that the completion of proper ADAS procedures serves as a liability risk control, Naikal said.

“Collision repair keeps getting more complex, and shops are being asked to take responsibility for increasingly sophisticated vehicle systems,” Bill Strout, president of Intrepid Direct, says in a press release. “This program gives our customers an easy way to build systematic ADAS review into their estimating and repair workflows through Kinetic ID Premium. Just as important, it creates a way to recognize shops that consistently identify and complete the right ADAS procedures, because those practices help reduce repair risk.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Through the use of Kinetic ID software, collision shops can qualify for additional liability and umbrella premium discounts, Naikal said. He adds that Intrepid Direct sees more use of the software and performance of ADAS calibrations as risk reducing behavior by the collision repair business.

“Their completed operations exposure goes down, and umbrella claims can go down,” Naikal adds. “Intrepid is recognizing that positive behavior and willing to reward that behavior with additional discounts.”
Identifying calibrations is important for vehicle repair, Naikal added.

“These sensors on the cars are no longer just convenience features,” he says. “They’re safety features. A vehicle that’s driving down the freeway at 60 miles per hour with a miscalibrated lane-keeping or lane-assist sensor behind the windshield or a blind spot monitoring system that doesn’t alert oncoming traffic in an adjacent lane can cause an accident and can be life-threatening for both the driver and passengers as well as the other vehicle.”
Failing to calibrate sensors can leave a vehicle not returned to its original state of safety, Naikal adds.
Naikal notes that Kinetic is a starting point that repair shops should use.

“The repairer is the one who has to make these decisions, and it could be nuanced,” Naikal said. “It could be circumstances and instances that they would choose to go one way or the other. Our idea with the software is to give them a starting point on the research and on where to go look.”

The partnership is a sign that the broader industry is recognizing good repair behavior, he adds. Shops that bring vehicles back to the factory state of safety will be rewarded for that behavior, he says.
“This is a good thing that the broader industry is starting to recognize shops that go the extra mile and make sure that the cars are repaired correctly,” Naikal says.

During a Collision Industry Conference meeting earlier this year, Rebekah Cooper, The Cooper Firm partner, explained how improper repairs, including those that involve ADAS systems, can be deadly or cause serious injuries.

Improper repair cases are changing as more emerging technology, such as ADAS features, become prominent on vehicles, she said. She said the legal system currently sees dozens of ADAS cases annually and that number is expected to increase.
She told the story of a case where a repair involving a bumper necessitated a calibration that wasn’t completed by the repair shop.

The firm discovered this by looking at what technology was on the vehicle and the repair procedures to see how it’s supposed to be repaired. They tracked the vehicle back to the last place it was repaired. It was discovered the business didn’t do the needed repair, she said.

The failed repair caused the collision warning not to work, she said. The consumer was quadriplegic following the crash. She lived in a mobile home for three years waiting for accountability, Cooper added.

“There are times we ask a shop for those, and the OEM has it, but the shop does not,” Cooper said. “Have you seen this before? When is the first time? Are you seeing it for the first time right now? If the answer is yes, that’s a problem.”

Intrepid and Kinetic’s new program will also give Intrepid Direct collision repair customers a limited-time free trial of Kinetic ID Premium and provide Kinetic network shops with access to Intrepid Direct insurance.
The program will kick off with Kinetic and Intrepid Direct co-hosting an event at Wynn Las Vegas Tuesday, Nov. 3 at 6 p.m. during the SEMA Show.
The Society of Collision Repair Specialists’ (SCRS) 2026 OEM Collision Repair Technology Summit will dive into a conversation about ADAS and calibrations during the SEMA Show next week.

The afternoon begins with “The National Safety Objective: Safer Vehicles, Safer Roads,” featuring National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) Deputy Administrator Lee White, who will examine federal vehicle and roadway safety priorities.

The session, held Thursday, Nov. 5 from 12:30-1:30 p.m., will include a conversation about emerging transportation technologies, data-driven research, and the federal government’s work with the industry to reduce fatalities and serious injuries, an SCRS release states.

During the “Engineering the Safety Benefit: From Requirements to Real-World Performance” session, active safety engineers from General Motors and Rivian will provide a look behind the engineering decisions that influence vehicle safety before, during, and after a collision.

The session, held Thursday, Nov. 5, from 2–3 p.m., will explore ADAS feature development, real-world effectiveness, crash avoidance and mitigation, implications of inoperable systems, verification of safety performance, and the potential for system degradation.

A session that follows, “Preserving the Driver Assistance System: Sensors, Calibration and Repairability,” will include service engineering experts from General Motors, Ford Motor Co., and Rivian. The conversation will answer for repairers what it takes to preserve and restore ADAS capabilities engineered into the vehicle after collisions.
The session, held Thursday, Nov. 5, from 3:30–4:30 p.m., will also take attendees behind the development of collision repair information.
The 2026 OEM Collision Repair Technology Summit is part of SCRS’ Repairer Driven Education (RDE) program at the SEMA Show, which includes several classes, the IDEAS Collide Showcase, and more.
